analysis: The only change in this PR is at StandaloneServerTests.swift line 663. A test-only stub LanguageModel's prepare signature moves from (input, cache, windowSize) to (input, cache, state: LMOutput.State?, prefill: PrefillParameters). This tracks an upstream mlx-swift-lm protocol change. The stub is private to the test target and returns .tokens(input.text). It touches no production code, no coordinator/provider WebSocket contract (TB-002), no key custody (A-003), no attestation or App Attest authorization (TB-009/TB-011), and no prefix-cache storage (T-041). The rest of the file (v2 slot construction and KV re-slice, MTP Prometheus rendering, setModels reslicing) is unchanged context, and I saw nothing in it that is security-relevant. The tests create fake HF snapshot directories under the user's cache and delete them afterwards, which is existing test behavior. One open question is outside this batch. The production LanguageModel conformances and the prefill/state parameters that now exist upstream (PrefillParameters, LMOutput.State) could affect the prefix-cache/KV paths covered by T-041 (SSD cache, KV state handling). This test change does not show what they do, so the next pass should check those production call sites only if the dependency bump is part of the PR. No security regression or new attack surface is identified in the supplied evidence.
